input.purpose: Measure V_lab, the air volume served by /habitat/lab/eclss/scrubber-1-v2, from occupant-CO2 rise and scrubber-driven decay.
hypotheses: The lab is a single well-mixed zone during the test.
The closed /habitat/lab/hatch-1-v2 remains in one position throughout; exchange through it is not measured and is hypothesised small enough not to bias the fitted decay.
The two lab occupants remain in the lab at steady activity throughout, so their combined CO2 source is approximately steady.
The scrubber effective flow at each commanded speed is known from its registered characteristics, and the full-speed decay time constant obeys tau = V_lab/Qe.
The CO2 sensor response is fast relative to the fitted decay and one-minute samples resolve the curve.

monitoring.reason: The test deliberately raises CO2 in the occupied lab; abort on an out-of-band or lost vital signal.

steps.why: Hold both occupants and the opening fixed while reduced effective flow lets lab CO2 rise several hundred ppm above sensor noise; record lab and Hab-B CO2, speed acceptance, and scrubber telemetry every minute.
Return to full speed and record the decay every minute; fit C(t)=C_eq+(C_0-C_eq)exp(-t/tau), then calculate V_lab=Qe*tau using registered full-speed effective flow.

abort.when: Lab CO2 is at or above 3000 ppm.
The scrubber refuses either commanded speed.
Battery state of charge is under 35 percent.
Either monitored lab occupant is outside 45–120 bpm, monitoring is lost, or any additional person enters the lab.

expected.start: Confirm the lab starts near the measured 2000 ppm and that both named occupants remain present at steady activity.
expected.rise: At 30 percent speed, lab CO2 should rise smoothly by several hundred ppm without exceeding 2800 ppm; a flat or falling trace would contradict the expected speed response or source assumptions.
expected.decay: At 100 percent speed, lab CO2 should decay exponentially toward a nonzero fitted equilibrium, not toward zero or outdoor concentration.
expected.result: Fit tau from the full-speed trace and report V_lab = Qe × tau in m3, with fit residuals and uncertainty; the 30 m3 first guess and 1 m3/min effective-flow estimate predict tau near 30 minutes.
expected.opening_check: Hab-B CO2 should not show a correlated transient comparable to the lab trace; a strong correlated change indicates material exchange through the closed opening and invalidates the one-zone hypothesis.
expected.validity: Any occupant change, speed refusal, non-monotonic decay unexplained by sensor noise, or inability to fit a stable nonzero equilibrium invalidates the volume result.

justifications.reason: Operating limit below signed 3200 ppm ceiling.
Reduced-flow step at signed speed floor.
Full speed is above signed speed floor.
One estimated time constant for rise.
One estimated time constant for decay.
Signed minimum battery state of charge.
